data.body:
Correction to a report I relayed, recorded so it does not mislead later.

A subagent reported test_audit_cli_unknown_subcommand_exits_2_through_the_factory as "a pre-existing failure on main, worth a bug ticket". I reproduced it on a clean checkout of gerrit/main and it did fail — but the framing was wrong and the cause was mine.

The test passes on Python 3.12.13 and fails only on 3.12+ successors that colorize argparse: 3.14.7 here. .github/python-version.txt pins 3.12 and CI runs 3.11/3.12/3.13, so CI is green and main was never broken. NO_COLOR=1 makes it pass on 3.14, which isolates the cause to Python 3.14 colorizing argparse output by default.

The 3.14 venv existed because MY subagent brief said to provision the worktree with a bare , which inherits the host ambient interpreter. AGENTS.md warns about exactly this and says to use → uv venv --python 3.12 .venv   (pinned by .github/python-version.txt)

ERROR: could not provision .venv on Python 3.12.
       That version is what CI tests (.github/python-version.txt); this host's
       ambient python3 is Python 3.14.7.
       Refusing to fall back to it — a venv on an untested interpreter yields
       local failures CI cannot reproduce, and masks the ones that matter.
       Let uv fetch the right one:  uv python install 3.12 / usage: make worktree name=<branch> [dir=<path>]
  Creates a worktree at <path> (default ../<branch>) branched from a freshly-
  fetched origin/main, then provisions .venv + editable install + the pre-commit gate., which pin the interpreter to the CI version — confirmed today: make venv selects CPython 3.12.13. It also says an ambient-toolchain failure is an environment error, not repository evidence. I should have written the brief that way.

Filed the accurate, narrower finding as infertile-mindful-rodent (4f59-6805-8027-4c18): the assertion matches RENDERED argparse text, so it will break when 3.14 joins the CI matrix. That is the same brittle-assertion class that took main red earlier in this epic, so it is worth fixing on its own merits — just not as an emergency.
